summary: Check-in for upcoming renewal at end of Nov. Pinegate wants to extend contract and pilot EU private/on-prem pathway for data residency. Discussed capacity uplift options (dedicated vs private), latency/cost tradeoffs, security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO), and a short benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing + amendment, SE to run pilot, Pinegate to provide token profile and legal timeline.
topics: EU data residency: Private/on-prem pilot requirements
Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security and compliance: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I see Oliver, Leena, Marco?
[00:08] Oliver (Pinegate): Yep, here — sorry ran late, had back-to-back with infra.
[00:12] Leena (Pinegate): Leena here.
[00:14] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus on the line. Good to meet you all.
[00:18] Sofia: Agenda is short — renewal timing, EU privacy pathway and a small on-prem pilot for the next quarter, and a pricing amendment for the commitment bump. Does that sound right?
[00:28] Marco (Pinegate): Yeah, that's right. We want to extend through q1 and add EU-only residency for a subset of traffic.
[00:34] Oliver: To be clear, it's not all traffic, mostly EU regulated customers — about 20 to 30% of requests today but growing.
[00:40] Leena: Also curious about latency, our internal SLOs are ~200ms p95 for inference; curious how Redwood Dedicated or Privet, sorry, Redwood Privet would hit that. (laughs)
[00:52] Marcus: (chuckle) Redwood Private — the product name — we can meet low-latency but it depends on model size and batching. For the EU on-prem we expect network egress to be minimal so latency can be within target for small-medium models.
[01:08] Sofia: Quick housekeeping — renewal date is Nov 30 2028, current commit runs out then. You're asking for an amendment to add a pilot for EU private on-prem plus a capacity uplift of approx 40% reserved GPU hours, correct?
[01:20] Marco: Correct, our forecast shows peak growth during Black Friday period and a steady 2-3x Q/Q growth in EU user traffic.
[01:28] Oliver: We'll share the exact token numbers, but ballpark is 1.2B tokens / month currently across all regions, EU accounts for about 300M and ramps fast.
[01:38] Leena: Also the security ask — KMS integration with our key rotation, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, SSO via SAML — any blockers?
[01:46] Marcus: No blockers in principle. Private VPC/on-prem supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs can be pushed and we have a Splunk forwarding pattern we can share. SAML — we support SAML 2.0, though in some exports the config fields are named a bit differently, sometimes transcribed as Sam-L in our docs — we can provide a short runbook.
[02:02] Sofia: Good. So cost question — Pinegate usually is mindful of unit cost; can you talk through the tradeoff between Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private on-prem?
[02:10] Marcus: Sure. Dedicated reserved pools give predictable throughput and lower per-token cost because we amortize GPUs across workloads and use batching/K-V cash — I mean K-V cache — automatic prefix cache. Private on-prem adds operational overhead and initial setup but gives you data residency and full control; unit cost usually higher if you fully provision for peak, but we can propose burst/burst-broker and hybrid routing so non-EU traffic still uses hosted.
[02:34] Oliver: Hybrid routing sounds interesting. If we keep session affinity for EU regulated users pinned to the private cluster and fallback to dedicated hosted in emergencies, that's probably acceptable. How does failover work?
[02:44] Marcus: We have smart routing policies — region-first, latency-first, or cost-first. For pilot we'd propose region-first with an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in a nearby region, with throttles to avoid cost shock. Canary rollouts for the pilot too.
[02:56] Marco: On compatibility, will quantized variants behave the same? We rely on consistent outputs.
[03:02] Marcus: Good point. We recommend locking a model family and running a diff-eval between the quantized and full-precision variants as part of the pilot. Redwood Optimize can help flag regressions against your eval set.
[03:12] Leena: How long is the pilot you usually run? A week? Two?
[03:14] Marcus: Typical pilot bench is 1–2 weeks of steady-state plus a small spike test. We'll collect latency, error rates, token cost, and output quality metrics. For contract purposes we run the pilot in a staging EU data center that matches your network topology.
[03:28] Sofia: Timeline-wise, Marcus — can you have a pilot harness and checklist ready to run week of Oct 16? That would give us results before the Nov 30 renewal.
[03:36] Marcus: Yes, we can. I can prep the harness and a short-run playbook by Oct 15.
[03:40] Oliver: Ok that's tight but sounds doable. On the pricing amendment: we want a 12-month extension with a step-up committed units schedule and an option to convert the pilot to a permanent private cluster if it passes.
[03:52] Sofia: We can build a contract amendment with a conversion clause — typical structure is a 6-week pilot clause and an option to convert with a 60-day notice and pre-agreed pricing. We'll draft numbers in the workbook.
[04:02] Marco: Also need to loop in procurement — any pre-reqs we should flag? e.g., SLAs for private deployments, uptime, support tiers.
[04:10] Sofia: For private we offer a premium support tier and an SLA tied to node availability for the private cluster. We'll include the SLA language in the draft amendment.
[04:18] Leena: One more infra detail — our current infra uses GCP europe-west1 and we prefer physical on-prem near FRA for latency. Is Redwood able to stage in a colocation or require partner cloud region?
[04:30] Marcus: We support on-prem and colocations. For the pilot, we can spin up a private cluster in a partner colo in FRA region; if you want fully air-gapped, that requires additional planning and infra packaging but we've done it with a couple of customers.
[04:44] Oliver: Security will push back on networking egress rules and key custody. If we do customer KMS we need HSM-backed keys and rotation logs.
[04:52] Marcus: That aligns with our private offering; we can do HSM-backed KMS and export audit trails to your Splunk instance or S3 logs with encryption. Expect an engineering window for key integration — about 2 weeks of coordination.
[05:06] Sofia: Let's talk numbers briefly: if we shift 300M tokens/month to EU private and reserve 40% more capacity overall, what's a rough delta to committed spend?
[05:16] Marcus: Off the cuff, private per-token cost is typically 10–25% above dedicated hosted, depending on utilization. If you convert pilot to long-term and opt for reserved nodes we can narrow that delta. We'll model this in the workbook — need exact token profiles to be accurate.
[05:30] Leena: We'll get those numbers out. Also curious about burst: can we have a burst broker so we don't overprovision for Black Friday?
[05:38] Marcus: Yes — burst broker is standard: you keep reserved nodes for steady baseline and we allow burst to hosted capacity or to a global pool. There's throttling and priority rules. We'll include a sample policy.
[05:50] Oliver: Ok good. Can you also surface any previous customer references that did a similar EU private pilot? Helps with procurement.
[05:58] Sofia: We can share anonymized references and a short case study. I'll attach the security pack and a one-pager on private pilots in the followup — links only, not full docs in the transcript.
[06:08] Leena: Perfect. On the model side: we use GL-3 family models for most production. Are there any known performance tweaks — kernel selection, quantization profiles — we should anticipate?
[06:20] Marcus: For GL-3 sized models we recommend int8 quantization for stable perf; kernel tuning depends on sequence length. Our runtime chooses kernels but for on-prem we'll preselect optimized kernels based on your token distribution. Also continuous batching works well with steady traffic; if you have many short queries we might tune small-window batching to keep latency low.
[06:40] Oliver: That sounds reasonable. Can Redwood's optimize recommendations be run against our dev traces?
[06:46] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Optimize can ingest anonymized traces and produce batching/quantization recommendations. We'll need a sanitized export.
[06:54] Marco: Legal will want data residency proof points and a controls mapping to SOC2. Do you have a controls matrix we can drop into our security review?
[07:02] Marcus: Yes — we have a controls mapping doc for Dedicated and Private with SOC2 alignment. We'll attach that in the security package. Note: some of the wordings in the matrix have typos in older exports — we keep an updated runbook.
[07:14] Leena: Quick clarification — audit log retention in Private: can we set retention policies? We prefer 7 years for some events but that might be overkill.
[07:22] Marcus: Retention is configurable, and logs can be exported to your S3 with lifecycle rules. We'd add that to the plan.
[07:30] Sofia: Anything else on compliance?
[07:32] Oliver: No, that's the main list.
[07:34] Sofia: Ok timeline recap: Pinegate to share token profile by Oct 11, Redwood to send pricing + amendment by Oct 12, SE to prepare pilot harness by Oct 15 and run pilot week of Oct 16 — results in time for negotiation before Nov 30. Legal readout by Oct 19. Sound accurate?
[07:50] Marco: Yes. Also please include a clause about conversion pricing in the amendment, so procurement doesn't need to renegotiate after pilot.
[07:58] Sofia: We'll include pre-agreed conversion pricing with a small premium to reflect private op costs.
[08:04] Leena: One more ops question — who manages OS/kernel patches for on-prem nodes in the private cluster?
[08:12] Marcus: For colocation/private we offer an ops-managed option or customer-managed. For the pilot we recommend Redwood-managed to reduce lift; once stable you can elect to take over with a runbook.
[08:24] Oliver: Redwood-managed works for us for pilot.
[08:26] Sofia: Great. I'll summarize action items here — Marcus will share the pilot checklist and harness, I'll send the contract amendment and pricing workbook, and Pinegate shares token logs.
[08:38] Marcus: I'll also include a short script to produce the token/time-of-day profile if you want to automate it.
[08:44] Oliver: That'd be helpful.
[08:46] (brief crosstalk)
[08:50] Sofia: Any open risks? From Redwood side: coordination for KMS and HSM, and pilot scheduling. From Pinegate: legal timeline and exact token profile. Any other risks?
[09:02] Marco: Procurement might push back on conversion price, but we'll try to lock it.
[09:06] Sofia: We'll propose a signed option in the amendment to address that.
[09:10] Leena: Ok.
[09:12] Sofia: Last thing — do you want a short demo or technical deep dive after the pilot results?
[09:18] Oliver: Probably a technical deep dive with our infra team.
[09:22] Sofia: Great, we'll schedule it after the pilot readout. I'll follow up with calendar invites.
[09:28] (meeting winds down; small talk)
[09:40] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up on the action items.
[09:44] Oliver: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Marcus: Thanks.
[09:47] (call ends)
